Redwood: provide SOC 2 Type II report and KMS integration notes (Ben)
Customer: review SLA targets and confirm uptime target range (Maya)
Schedule legal-to-legal call for week of May 4th

Ben Kapoor | Attach SOC2 report and architecture diagram showing KMS/HSM and VPC options | 2026-05-01

header:
Date: 2026-04-28 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alice Thompson (Redwood AE), Ben Kapoor (Redwood SE), Lina Morales (Redwood CSM); Maya Lin (Acme Procurement), Jordan Reyes (Acme Legal), Samir Patel (Acme Security), Tina Ho (Acme Platform)
Meeting purpose: Align on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA targets, pricing commitments, and next steps for vendor onboarding and security review.
summary: Short call to triage outstanding procurement and legal questions before the commercial approval. Main threads: liability and indemnity caps in the MSA, DPA specifics around data residency and processing, SLA uptime/latency targets tied to pricing tiers, SOC2/HIPAA evidence and KMS/HSM support for key management, and scheduling a legal-to-legal review. Action items captured and a follow-up legal sync targeted for early May.
transcript:
[00:00] Alice Thompson (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining on short notice, i'm Alice from Redwood inference, i'll kick us off
[00:07] Maya Lin (Acme - Procurement): hi thanks, Maya here, appreciate it, we have about 45 minutes and a few stakeholders on the legal security side
[00:15] Ben Kapoor (Redwood SE): hey all, ben from redwood, happy to cover the technical items, especially SOC2 and KMS integration notes
[00:22] Jordan Reyes (Acme - Legal): Jordan, legal — we'll be mainly focused on indemnity, liability caps, and DPA specifics today
[00:28] Tina Ho (Acme - Platform): tina — i'll chime in for platform questions around VPC and routing, and latency SLAs
[00:34] Alice: cool quick agenda: 1) MSA redlines high-level, 2) DPA/data residency, 3) SLA targets vs pricing, 4) SOC2/KMS evidence, 5) next steps. if that sounds good we'll jump in
[00:45] Maya: yep sounds good
[00:50] Jordan: fine
[00:52] Alice: first on the MSA, we circulated a version last week, i flagged the standard redwood positions — liability cap at the greater of $5M or 2x paid fees, indemnity limited to third-party ip claims, and termination for convenience with 30 days notice. any immediate blockers from your side?
[01:12] Jordan: yeah so two quick points — acme legal typically asks for a higher liability cap for core infra vendors, and we need a carve-out for breaches involving customer data. can you explain how your DPA ties into that?
[01:26] Alice: sure — the DPA maps to the MSA and we can scope the cap carve-out limited to gross negligence or intentional misconduct, we don't usually accept unlimited liability. our suggested path is an exception for specific data breach scenarios tied to proven failure in encryption or key management.
[01:44] Jordan: okay that's helpful; we'll likely propose language to clarify which events trigger the carve-out. we'll want to loop in procurement for acceptability though
[01:52] Maya: from procurement perspective, our escalation matrix requires legal sign-off if the cap is below $10M for platform providers, but there's room if we get stronger SLA credits and incident response SLAs.
[02:05] Ben: on incident response, we have a SOC2 Type II, 24/7 on-call for Sev 1, and playbooks for incident triage. we log audit trails in the console and can provide exportable audit logs.
[02:19] Samir Patel (Acme - Security): can you confirm what you retain in logs? we need fips-compliant encryption for keys and bring-your-own-key via KMS/HSM is a requirement for some of our regulated stores
[02:31] Ben: yes we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) via KMS integrations, and HSM-backed keys for private deployments, for hosted we offer tenant encryption with keys managed by the customer in supported clouds; i'll attach a diagram after.
[02:44] Tina: how about data residency — some of our data must remain in eu-west-1 and can't be transited through other regions
[02:51] Alice: we have region pinning for model serving and storage; in Dedicated/Private we can guarantee region residency and single-tenant options. for hosted API we can route to a eu region and set retention rules, though contractual residency guarantees are typically part of private deals.
[03:08] Jordan: on the DPA side, we have a few custom requests: subprocessors list, deletion guarantees, and audit rights — specifically a right to audit logs for 3rd party assessments. are those feasible?
[03:21] Ben: subprocessors — we provide a list and 30-days notice for changes, deletion — we can provide deletion APIs and attestations within agreed windows, audit rights — we can provide SOC2 reports and scoped audit access for an agreed cadence; full on-site audits for hosted products are harder but for Dedicated/Private we can accommodate tighter audit rights.
[03:45] Maya: great, procurement will want that spelled out in the DPA appendix because it affects our risk scoring
[03:52] Alice: noted. next topic SLA. what are your expected uptime and latency SLOs and how do they map to credits or termination triggers?
[04:03] Tina: for interactive customer features we need 99.9% availability across the model endpoints and p95 latency below 500ms for short prompts. if latency degrades consistently we will need credits or automatic failover to a cheaper model variant.
[04:19] Ben: 99.9% is achievable on Dedicated and Private; on hosted api our public SLO is 99.5% with best-effort latency commitments and documented regional performance numbers. we can create a custom SLA in the contract for an uplift to 99.9% tied to reserved capacity or committed monthly spend.
[04:37] Maya: that maps to cost — do you have pricing bands for committed throughput vs burst?
[04:43] Alice: yes we have Reserved/Dedicated tiers that include reserved GPU pools, autoscaling policies, and priority routing. pricing is a blended model: base monthly commit + per-token overage. we'll propose a pricing worksheet showing SKU-level costs for different commit levels.
[04:58] Jordan: we also need clarity on service credits — is it pro rata or financial credit and how is it calculated?
[05:05] Ben: service credits are typically a percentage of the monthly invoice tied to SLO misses. we can include a formula in the SLA appendix. for Dedicated we also add an operational runbook and faster incident response SLA.
[05:19] Samir: one more security Q — what controls around prompt telemetry and embeddings do you provide? we don't want raw customer prompts stored long-term and embeddings accessible to other tenants
[05:30] Ben: by default we persist prompts for short-term caching to improve latency but we offer opt-out retention policies; embeddings for host-model caching are tenant-scoped and never exposed to other tenants. for customers needing maximum isolation we recommend Dedicated/Private and BYOK.
[05:50] Jordan: ok re: indemnity — earlier you mentioned ip indemnity limited to third-party claims. our standard asks for broader indemnities for data breach impacts; is there wiggle room?
[06:02] Alice: we can expand indemnity but will need to keep it tied to direct damages and exclude consequential loss; we typically cap aggregate liability as discussed. we can negotiate some carve-outs if commercial terms meet thresholds.
[06:17] Maya: procurement note — if we can get a 99.9% SLA and a 12-month commit at tier 2 pricing, procurement can escalate for approval quicker. otherwise it'll go into extended review.
[06:31] Alice: understood. we'll draft two options in the commercial worksheet: one with 99.9% on Dedicated and a 12-month commit, and a hosted option at 99.5% with no commit.
[06:44] Jordan: can you also include termination assistance and data export guarantees? that's important for our offboarding process
[06:52] Ben: yes termination assistance — we provide export tooling and a 90-day runbook for data extraction and assistance. for Private we can do longer handover windows.
[07:03] Tina: regarding compliance evidence, SOC2 is one thing but for certain accounts we need HIPAA BAAs. do you support BAAs?
[07:12] Alice: we offer BAAs for eligible customers under Private or Dedicated contracts; for hosted API there's a review process. we'll include BAA scoping in the legal-to-legal conversation.
[07:24] Jordan: on subprocessors, do you list cloud providers and any managed service partners? we need full transparency in the DPA
[07:31] Ben: yes list includes major cloud providers and our managed infra partners; we'll provide the current subprocessors list and an update cadence.
[07:38] Maya: timeline — procurement is targeting vendor onboarding by mid-may. is that realistic if legal exceptions take a couple weeks?
[07:47] Alice: if we get agreement on key commercial points and legal-to-legal happens early the week of may 4th, mid-may onboarding is feasible. it depends on final redlines on the MSA and the commit level.
[07:59] Jordan: we'll prepare proposed redlines and the DPA exceptions list. want redwood to come back with a tracked MSA that highlights the liability and indemnity language.
[08:09] Alice: we'll do that. ben will attach the SOC2 and KMS notes. lina will coordinate the legal-to-legal scheduling.
[08:18] Lina Morales (Redwood CSM): i'll send calendar options for the week of may 4th and own the meeting invite
[08:23] Samir: small technical point — for latency SLOs, do you offer regional failover so requests from eu are not routed to us-east during incidents?
[08:33] Ben: yes region pinning + smart routing is available in Dedicated/Private; for hosted we do regional routing but not guaranteed single-region isolation unless in a Private instance.
[08:45] Jordan: also need to confirm data deletion certification — is there an attestation we can embed in DPA post-termination?
[08:53] Ben: yes we can provide deletion attestations and logs showing deletion operations.
[08:57] Maya: ok good. from procurement side we'll need the pricing worksheet and the two commercial options to evaluate cost impact; please include headcount and token assumptions for our avg and peak workloads
[09:13] Alice: will do. anything else on legal side?
[09:17] Jordan: on indemnity and liability we'll send proposed language, and we expect redwood to respond with counter-language before the legal-to-legal.
[09:27] Alice: understood. quick recap of action items and owners: alice will send tracked MSA draft, ben will send SOC2 & architecture/KMS note, lina will schedule legal-to-legal, acme will provide DPA exceptions and sla preferences.
[09:42] Maya: sounds right. procurement will push to streamline if the 12-month commit option is reasonable
[09:49] Tina: one last platform ask — can you provide historical latency percentiles for eu-west-1 for similar customers? we want empirical evidence
[09:58] Ben: i can anonymize and share p50/p95/p99 for comparable workloads; i'll include that with the performance appendix.
[10:07] Alice: great. we are aligned on next steps and we'll follow up with documents. thanks everyone for your time.
[10:15] Jordan: thanks
[10:16] Samir: thanks
[10:17] Maya: bye
[10:20] [call ends]
